decision_boundary: This record selects a bounded pilot lane for future scaffold work only. It is not a simulator run, target-cost selection, rate calculation, rate publication, public rate card, tax proposal, savings estimate, waste finding, fraud finding, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, solver result, outcome-floor threshold decision, or balanced-budget claim.

selected_pilot.selected_scope: transportation asset maintenance and safety pilot scaffold
selected_pilot.selection_rationale: The transportation asset-maintenance and safety candidate is narrow, has existing trust-fund/accounting boundaries, can keep federal grants and state/local delivery separate, has observable safety and asset-condition floor families, and avoids immediate tax-distribution, benefit-adequacy, statutory-continuity, health-incidence, or fraud/savings choices.

criteria_results.reason: Asset maintenance and safety can be scoped below the full transportation lane.
The selection does not choose a tax distribution, benefit adequacy rule, statutory continuity rule, or target level.
Prior transportation depth work indicates plausible official-source families, but this decision does not capture new source bytes or close custody.
Safety, asset condition, access, reliability, equity, resilience, and delivery-feasibility families can be specified without setting thresholds in this pulse.
Maintenance planning, project delivery, inspection, and asset-inventory modernization can be modeled as transition paths with implementation cost and stress cases.
The pilot can remain deterministic and narrow without revenue-package optimization.
The pilot can be described as asset-maintenance and safety readiness, not waste, fraud, recoverable savings, causal savings, or a department cut.

non_selected_candidates.reason: Reserve rules and avoided-loss boundaries are more exposed to emergency and stress-parameter choices, so this remains a later candidate.
Claims modernization remains useful, but payment-integrity language has higher fraud, recoverability, and causal-savings confusion risk for the first simulator.

role_review_summary.finding: Selection does not publish a rate, burden, or taxpayer allocation and keeps future fairness analysis blocked.
Selection preserves transportation trust-fund, general-fund, state/local, offset, and reconciliation boundaries.
Future simulator inputs require official source custody, matched period, byte count, SHA-256, and metadata; no new source is captured here.
Selection keeps maintenance, safety, access, resilience, project delivery, and public-good service floors separate from rate claims.
No lower-cost recognition is allowed until access, quality/safety, equity, adequacy/resilience, delivery feasibility, and lane-specific floors pass.
Selection does not create a filing, withholding, fee, user-charge, employer, taxpayer, or agency compliance burden.
Selection does not alter fund balances, reserves, debt, net interest, deficit gap, or balanced-budget status.
Selection is narrow and falsifiable; it avoids proof rhetoric, savings language, waste language, and technology-cut shortcuts.

next_required_artifacts.purpose: Name official source families, retrieval metadata requirements, custody fields, and matched period/unit/perimeter needs.
Define the current-law transportation asset-maintenance and safety baseline without reform deltas.
Define access, quality/safety, equity, adequacy/resilience, delivery-feasibility, and lane-specific floor indicators without setting thresholds yet.
Define transition-cost, measured-productivity, implementation-risk, fallback, and stress fields before any technology effect.
